findings.reason: the state-machine specification must either feed the synthesized v0.0.0 baseline to both stable queries or forbid `--bump` before a real stable tag exists, since today a new machine's first `--bump` raises where §18 presents the machine as complete.
findings.text: §18 adds "with no semver tag, the package is stable at v0.0.0", but that synthesized baseline is described only for the latest-tag query; `_get_latest_stable_tag` (imas_codex/cli/release.py:45) reads the same v-filtered list and, on a package whose only tag is a stable-less `v0.0.1-rc1`, returns None, so the copied machine's abandon-RC path (`stable_tag = _get_latest_stable_tag()` then `raise click.ClickException("No stable (non-RC) tags found to bump from...")`, imas_codex/cli/release.py:223-228) raises for a fresh machine that §18 tells a coordinator to release with `--bump`. The instances are both stable-baseline queries, not one: `_get_latest_tag` at imas_codex/cli/release.py:29 is covered by the starting state, `_get_latest_stable_tag` at imas_codex/cli/release.py:45 is not

findings.reason: the lead must name `maps/<machine>/` (the `paths.py` owner) or the plan's own summary contradicts the section that moved the maps.
findings.text: the lead paragraph places the maps at `/work/projects/imas_gpu/jt60sa/maps/`, but §17 moved them to `maps/<machine>/` owned by `imas_ambix/data/paths.py:35` (`MAPS_DIR`) and states "take the maps back out of /work"; `ls /work/projects/imas_gpu/jt60sa/maps` now fails. The placement is written in two places — the lead and the §17/`paths.py` owner — and they disagree, so a reader of the plan summary is sent to a directory that no longer exists

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `imas_ambix/maps_cli.py` hides the registry auth, the tag list and its semver sort, the two-state version machine, the tree digest and the push behind the three `maps` commands; the four registry helpers and `compute_next_version` are copied into one module rather than spread across wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the map directory is stated in two places that have drifted: the plan's own lead still places the maps under `/work/projects/imas_gpu/jt60sa/maps/`, while §17 moves them to `maps/<machine>/` owned by `imas_ambix/data/paths.py:35` and that principal path is already gone.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; the section's "Accounting for the new surface" paragraph names what the `maps` group merges (the installer's private `oras pull`) and why the one added refusal cannot be retired (the tree it guards is the only copy of unreleased work), so the added CLI surface and refusal are accounted for.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan enumerates every registry tag query of the copied machine (`_get_latest_tag`, `_get_latest_stable_tag`, `_tag_exists`) yet its new "no semver tag → stable at v0.0.0" starting state covers only `_get_latest_tag`; `_get_latest_stable_tag` (imas_codex/cli/release.py:45), which the copied machine's abandon-RC `--bump` path calls at imas_codex/cli/release.py:223, is left unhandled and returns None on that same package state.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the only wrapper is `maps pull` over `oras pull`, and the plan states why the installer's private oras path cannot be extended and must instead be merged: the registry, the auth form and the artifact type then have one owner.
